top3.lead: Korea's KOSPI dropped 6.2% on Wednesday, its biggest fall in this run of AI worries.
top3.text: KOSPI closed at 4,697.51 after Wall Street's tech slump. Samsung fell 9.9% and SK hynix 11.1%. Korea is 16.2% of your portfolio, and the Bank of Korea decides on rates today.

stories.headline: KOSPI drops over 6% as AI worries return and Samsung and SK hynix slide
stories.what: KOSPI fell 308.52 points, or 6.16%, to 4,697.51 after touching 4,672.55. A tech slump on Wall Street revived doubts about how long the AI boom can last. Samsung Electronics lost 9.87% and SK hynix 11.05%. Foreign investors withdrew a net 1.9 trillion won. Decliners beat gainers 593 to 294, and the exchange paused programme orders for five minutes in the morning.
stories.why: Samsung and SK hynix are the heaviest names in Korean funds, so this drop reaches SCBKEQTG and EWY directly. This morning your dashboard prices SCBKEQTG at its 23 Nov NAV. KOSPI rose about 6% on 24 Nov, then fell on the 25th. By my calculation it ended roughly 0.2% below the 23 Nov level, so the next NAV may move little overall. A newer NAV may arrive at 11:30.
stories.verify_note: Single outlet; the 0.2% figure is my own calculation from the article

related.label: Today in Seoul
related.headline: Bank of Korea decides on rates
related.text: The base rate is 3%. A quarter-point rise to 3.25% is widely expected, according to a preview published on 22 Nov. Q3 growth was 3.4% against the bank's 2.6% forecast, while core inflation stayed at 2.8%. Samsung's large dividend is due to be paid on 27 Nov.

stories.headline: US stocks pare big AI-driven drop; tech funds feel it most
stories.what: The Nasdaq was down more than 4% at its low, and the Nasdaq 100 briefly fell 20% from its record close. It then recovered most of the loss. The Nasdaq Composite closed down 0.52% and the Dow rose 0.69%. Nvidia fell 4.7%. Reported causes were AI valuation worries, possible tighter AI regulation after the midterms, the new tariff proposal and rate-rise expectations.
stories.why: Your US exposure is mostly S&P 500 funds plus a few chip names, so a tech-led drop shows up there and in the semiconductor and AI funds. Futures were lower this morning: S&P 500 down 0.42% and Nasdaq-100 down 1.05%. Several US funds are priced at their 23 Nov NAV, so this drop is not in those numbers yet.
stories.verify_note: Two outlets agree on the swing; index closes differ slightly by outlet

related.label: Credit worries
related.headline: AI borrowing under scrutiny
related.text: Bloomberg reported that credit-risk gauges for CoreWeave and Nvidia reached record highs on Wednesday, as investors worry about heavy borrowing to fund AI spending.

stories.headline: Hot US inflation keeps a December Fed rate rise expected
stories.what: Core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, rose 0.3% in October and 3.3% from a year earlier. That is its highest annual rate in three years, up from 3.1% in September. Consumer spending grew 4.2% in the third quarter. Markets expect the Fed to raise rates at its 8-9 December meeting, and again in early 2027.
stories.why: Higher rates weigh on stock valuations, especially richly priced tech, which is part of why Wednesday's AI worries hit so hard. A rate rise also tends to pull Thai and Asian currencies and funds in the same direction. The US 10-year yield closed at 4.85%, down 6 basis points.
stories.verify_note: Two outlets agree on 0.3%; BEA release not checked

stories.headline: US proposes new overcapacity tariffs on 14 partners; Korea keeps its 15% cap
stories.what: The US proposed Section 301 tariffs on 14 partners over industrial overcapacity, including Korea, Japan, the EU, Taiwan, China, Thailand, Vietnam and Malaysia. Korea, Japan, the EU and Taiwan would stay at their 15% deal ceilings. China would face 20%, on top of existing duties. Public comment and hearings come first, and a start around January 2027 is possible. The China A50 index fell 1.45% in its last session.
stories.why: Korea's cap limits the new damage to Korean exporters. The proposal still names electronics, autos and ships. It also names Thailand and Vietnam, where final rates were not available to me. China is the exposed market, though it is only 3.6% of your portfolio.
stories.verify_note: Two outlets agree; Thai and Vietnam rates not found

briefly.headline: Thai SET index fell 1.6% on Wednesday
briefly.text: The SET closed at 1,428.50, down 1.59% on the dashboard's own data. I did not find a reported cause. Thailand is also among the 14 partners named in the tariff proposal, though its rate was not available to me. Thailand is 24.4% of your portfolio.
briefly.verify_note: Index level from dashboard data; cause not confirmed

briefly.headline: Gold swung hard, and sources disagree on where it stands
briefly.text: One report had spot gold down 3% to $3,445.89 at midday in New York, a low since August 2025, after the inflation data. The dashboard's futures tile instead shows a 0.74% gain at the close. I could not reconcile the two, so treat the level as unclear.
briefly.verify_note: Report and dashboard tile disagree; not reconciled

briefly.headline: Bitcoin dips below $60,000, then steadies
briefly.text: Bitcoin briefly slipped under $60,000 during the tech slump and ended near $60,134, up 0.65% over 24 hours. CoinDesk noted the Nasdaq's loss narrowed through the day.
briefly.verify_note: Single outlet; price from dashboard data
